title: Brother's blues, Vivian, and a band's players
summary: Garbled recollection of a player who could stop a dance with the blues, a woman player named Vivian, a clarinet-playing cousin Warren and other bandmates; he also mentions seeing Tony Sanders and playing with him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I have so many movies on the Boeber Street and behind the melody. You have a picture of Moonlight Serenade. Yeah, I have a little bit of things. He's tall as you and that.
You were saying that when Brother played the blues, first one or two came around and then... Everybody started. And they were just watching him...

That was the place, the first place I took a drink in my life. They were just watching him play. That's right. They enjoyed it so much. They enjoyed him and he was playing. I mean, he could... In other words, he could stop a dance when he got ready. Yeah. Yeah. And he left us and we picked up a woman by the name of Vivian from Atkins, Kansas. And she was very good paying up there too. She came up with a band that we came down there. And you know, until the band... Things like a little tough and bad. But she was a very good paying up there too. Someday I'd like you to get this band to play up from... Best listeners of Harry Faggner to it. Yeah, yeah. First player with Desdun and us. He could sing and play. Didn't have no mic, you know. If they weren't in a megaphone. Yeah. I mean, you can hear them all over the place. A little bit of things. And his cousin was playing with us at that time. Two out of... Let me see. I think he was playing in Lucian Johnson's place. I'm trying to... No. He was playing before Lucian Johnson. Very good clarinet. He played clarinet, piano and saxophone. His name is Warren. He's the one of that. And bass on that's where Patrick stands. Very, very good. And if you ever want to know something about Catherine, I'll tell you who's played Maddie Reyes, banjo. I can take it back by the skin field. Yeah. That's a good thing. Mm-hmm. But in them days, George Ganova was in there with him too, you know. Yeah, George was good. George always could play a band. He can still play a part of his son, yeah. Yeah.

Yeah, I went to Tony's house last night, Tony Sanders here, to his barber shop. He's still cutting hair. Tried to find it when I was playing with him on the Pelican, you know. I played several jobs with him on the Pelican. All I remember, Ellie Begarden was playing drum with him.
